title: NULL and three-valued logic
objective: NULL is not an ordinary value. Comparisons with NULL produce UNKNOWN, and WHERE keeps only predicates that evaluate to TRUE.
misconception: The starter checks due_on = NULL, which selects no overdue-unscheduled rows instead of matching NULL dates.
acceptance: Test the truth tables for TRUE AND UNKNOWN and FALSE AND UNKNOWN. Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL, and consider IS DISTINCT FROM when comparing nullable values without UNKNOWN.
securityBoundary: COALESCE can be useful for display, but replacing every NULL with a fake sentinel can corrupt business meaning.
